title: astra.registry.queue/1
description:
state/queue/<id>@<version>.json — a release waiting out its publication delay (contract B.4; registry plan BOT-38). The plugins service reads three members of it: `submission_id`, `decision_id` and `publish_after`.

THIS IS THE ONE RECORD IN schema/ THAT IS NOT CLOSED, AND THAT IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT. B.4's sentence for the queue entry fixes what OTHER PARTIES READ, not the whole member set — unlike `astra.registry.identity/1` ("exactly these required members") and DEC-7 ("with only these members"), which are closed and whose schemas set `additionalProperties` to false. The entry itself is BOT-33's publication queue and carries a dozen members besides: `id`, `version`, `repo`, `tag`, `submitter`, `queued_at`, `delay_hours`, `reason`, `artifact_digests`, `approved_by`, `approved_at`, `approved_for`, `issue` and a `$comment`, every one of them on `main` in the twenty-odd entries git has carried. Closing this object would refuse the file the bot actually writes. So `additionalProperties` is left open ON PURPOSE, and what this schema states is the floor the service depends on rather than the shape the bot happens to produce.

WHICH ENTRIES THIS APPLIES TO. Contract §214 records that today's entries carry neither id nor `schema`. tools/validate.mjs therefore judges an entry against this file only when the entry DECLARES itself one — that is, when it carries a `schema` member — and notes a pre-BOT-38 entry as the legacy shape rather than refusing it. An entry that claims `astra.registry.queue/1` and then omits `decision_id` is a different thing from an entry written before the member existed, and only the first is a defect.

`submission_id` IS NOT IN THIS FILE, AND THAT IS NOW AN UNWRITTEN ADDITION RATHER THAN A FACT THIS FILE IS WAITING ON. When this schema landed with B-T2.1, B.4 and the token file both recorded the member REQUIRED — schema/contract-tokens-v1.json was at contract_version 0.19.0 and listed it `"required": true` — and B-T2.1's exception, `submission_id` required only "unless the entry's registry-only `trigger` is legacy (`issue`, `ping`, `dispatch`, `legacy`)", was owed by a contract version that had not been published (§1.3 row 6). IT HAS BEEN PUBLISHED. Contract 0.20.0 of 2026-09-20 makes the member optional under B.4, and astra-registry `8e03da6` regenerated the token file the same day with `astra.registry.queue/1`.`submission_id` at `"required": false`, where every regeneration since has kept it.

SO WHAT IS LEFT IS NOT A WAIT BUT B-T3.10'S REGISTRY HALF, UNWRITTEN: a `properties` entry for `submission_id` carrying §0.7's UUID grammar and NOT required, and the legacy `trigger` conditional beside the decision record's in tools/validate.mjs, because tools/lib/jsonschema.mjs implements no `if`/`then`. Until that is written this file refuses no conforming entry — the object is open, so an entry carrying `submission_id` passes as it stands — and this paragraph is here so that the next reader takes the silence for neither an omission nor a wait. It read as a wait for two days and ten releases after the fact landed, because the claim was prose and the record that knew was machine-readable and nothing joined them; tools/selftest/contract-tokens.mjs joins them now (astra-plugins-ops dev/couplings.md, 53).

WHAT NOTHING HERE CAN CHECK. That `decision_id` names a decision record that exists, that `publish_after` is `queued_at` plus the delay the reason code implies, and BOT-38's "MUST carry no `issue` and, for a bound submission, no login in `submitter`" are all statements about other files or about a step, not about this one. The first two are bot/publish-apply.mjs's; the third is BOT-38's and is gated on the issue channel closing at R6, while every entry git carries today legitimately has an `issue`. Recorded as gaps rather than implied by this file's existence.

decision_id.$comment: DEC-7's `decision_id` for the decision that queued this release: §0.7's 32 lowercase hex (BOT-35). It is what joins the entry to the public log, which is the whole reason the service is given it.

publish_after.$comment: §0.7: RFC 3339 UTC, whole seconds, `Z`. The moment the release may be published; editing it is how a delay is brought forward by hand. The pattern cannot say the date is real; tools/validate.mjs round-trips it through Date.
